articles.title: Deadly fire at Canada military base moved a kilometre 'in 30 to 60 seconds'
articles.summary: The blaze that killed four men and injured dozens of others spread with alarming speed, accounts suggest.
articles.body:
The fire that killed four members of the Canadian military and injured dozens of others on Saturday spread with alarming speed, accounts suggest.

It broke out in a grassy training area at a base in the province of Alberta and spread rapidly due to strong winds.

"The fire was 1km (0.6 miles) away when the wind shifted," said Maj-Gen Wade Rutland, commander of the 1st Canadian Division of the Canadian Armed Forces. "It is not normal for a fire to move a kilometre in 30 to 60 seconds."

Prime Minister Mark Carney described it as "one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime". Officials have ruled out the possibility of "any terrorist activity".

The blaze began at about 16:00 (22:00 GMT) on Saturday at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, one of the country's busiest military training bases.

The BBC has confirmed that Sgt Morgan Wong, Pte Shaun Farrell, Pte Aidan Goulding and Pte Hayden Lykkemark have died.

Of the 39 injured people receiving care in hospital, at least 19 are in a critical condition.

Warren Thirsk, an emergency department doctor at the Royal Alexandra Hospital, told Canadian broadcaster CBC that the number of patients involved in the incident had "completely overwhelmed" healthcare facilities in Wainwright.

What we know so far about deadly fire at Canadian military base

Tributes are being paid to the servicemen who died.

Patricia Farrell, the mother of Shaun Farrell, wrote on Facebook that it was "with heavy hearts that we share the news that our son, Shaun Farrell, has passed away to be with our Heavenly Father".

Wong received a tribute from the Loyal Edmonton Regiment, of which he was part. The regiment was "deeply saddened", it wrote in a Facebook post of its own. It sent "heartfelt condolences to [the group's] families, friends, and fellow soldiers".

The mother of Goulding, Sonia Monk, said her late son was an exceptional athlete and a natural leader. "He was always the guy who kept everybody's spirits up," she told CBC. "He really was the light of my life."

In account of Saturday's events, Rutland told reporters that members of the infantry had been conducting "high-intensity combat training with live munitions" at a grenade range and attack range.

He told reporters that officials knew about the fire on the base for several hours, but it was decided that training "could carry on for a certain amount of time".

"I spoke to my commander last night, and he said within 30 seconds to a minute they saw no fire, and then there was a fire right on top of them," Rutland said.

Rutland said it was not yet known what exactly caused the fire.

Some witnesses had said they had heard explosions, fuelling speculation that oil and gas infrastructure may have been hit and sparked the fire. But Rutland said authorities "do not believe this [incident] to be a result of any oil and gas infrastructure".

The Canadian Armed Forces has said that "while the incident remains under investigation, at this time, there are no indications that it was the result of any terrorist activity".

Forecasters had issued a wind warning on Saturday for large parts of Alberta, predicting wind gusts of up to 90km/h (66mph), Canadian broadcaster CBS said.

According to Rutland, the investigation may take at least a month.

Wainwright, about 130 miles east of Edmonton, Alberta's capital, is one of the main bases used by the Canadian military for live-fire training exercises, and it houses troops from Canada and allied countries.

About 690 military personnel and 300 civilian workers are on site on a typical day.

articles.title: Cambridgeshire train attacker Anthony Williams admits wounding
articles.summary: Anthony Williams is in court after multiple stabbings on a train that was forced to stop in Huntingdon.
articles.body:
A man accused of a mass stabbing on a train in Cambridgeshire last year has pleaded guilty to 12 counts of wounding with intent.

Passengers and staff were injured on the 18:25 Doncaster-London service on Saturday, 1 November after it left Peterborough, causing it to make an unscheduled stop at Huntingdon railway station.

Anthony Williams, 33, has denied 14 counts of attempted murder, relating to the train and to incidents in London and Peterborough, and is due to stand trial next week.

Appearing at a pre-trial review at Cambridge Crown Court, Williams, of Langford Road in Peterborough, pleaded guilty to the lesser wounding charges and several other offences.

He appeared via video link from Rampton Hospital in Nottinghamshire.

At an earlier hearing, Williams pleaded not guilty to attempting to murder Jonathan Gjoshe, Sachin Balakrishnan, David Presland, Scott Bletcher, Scott Green, Kevin Deely, Stephen Crean, Raza Aslam, Michael Paffett, and Samir Zitouni on the train near Huntingdon on 1 November.

In front of Mr Justice Calver this Monday, Williams pleaded guilty to 12 counts of wounding with intent and two of attempting to wound with intent in relation to incidents on the train, and earlier in Peterborough and London.

He also admitted affray at a barber shop in Peterborough on 31 October and the theft of knives from an Asda store in Stevenage on 31 October.

He pleaded guilty to possessing a bladed article in a public place in Peterborough on 31 October, at Pontoon Dock DLR station at Silvertown, east London, in the early hours of 1 November, and on the train between Peterborough and Huntingdon on 1 November.

He also admitted assault occasioning actual bodily harm of a male police officer on 2 November, and common assault on a Govia Thames Link train between London St Pancras and Biggleswade in Bedfordshire on 1 November.

Prosecutor Christopher Paxton KC said the "guilty pleas do not resolve the indictment, so there will be a trial".

Williams also denies one count of attempted murder at Pontoon Dock DLR station on 1 November and three counts of attempted murder in Peterborough on 31 October.

The trial, which is expected to last six weeks, is due to begin next Monday.

articles.title: Adult children cutting off parents as some blame therapy for family estrangements
articles.summary: Richard Blake says therapy culture has raised the bar on parenting and may fuel parent-child estrangement through an overcorrection in cutoff culture.
articles.body: Amid a reported surge in parent-child estrangements, some have questioned whether therapy could play a role in the family fracture trend. Nearly four in 10 Americans are currently estranged from at least one close family member, according to a 2025 YouGov poll of 4,395 U.S. adults, including 24% from a sibling, 16% from a parent and 10% from a child. While therapy can be helpful in facilitating communication and mending relationships, some believe it could contribute to "cutoff culture." 5 REASONS MORE AMERICANS ARE CUTTING OFF THEIR OWN PARENTS, ACCORDING TO PSYCHOLOGIST In two recent large-scale surveys of over 5,200 U.S. parents who were estranged from adult children, 1,014 parents reported that their children began therapy within the year before the estrangement. Meanwhile, 515 parents reported that their adult children had indicated therapy influenced their decision about the relationship, and 1,254 said their child had received a mental health diagnosis. (The surveys were not peer-reviewed or nationally representative and relied on parents' accounts of their adult children’s experiences, limiting what can be concluded about therapy’s role in estrangement.) The therapy debate Richard Blake, Ph.D., a Texas-based psychology researcher with a focus on anxiety and family estrangement, refers to the trend as an "overcorrection" happening in today’s society. "There is a lot of debate online about whether it's happening or not," Blake, who was a researcher in the surveys referenced above and has written a book about how therapy could be fueling family estrangement, told Fox News Digital. "I hear it from both sides. I hear from parents who say, ‘My child said my therapist should cut you off,’ and people who've told me, ‘My therapist told me I should cut my parents off.’ How much it's happening and when it's appropriate and inappropriate is where the nuance comes in." Laura Wellington, a Connecticut mother who has been estranged from her adult daughter since 2024, also weighed in on the potential role therapists play in the growing divide. "Therapy has sort of raised the bar of what is good enough parenting." "Do therapists, in my opinion, play a role in the estrangement epidemic? 100%," she told Fox News Digital. "But that doesn't mean there aren't some really good therapists out there." Wellington, known on social media as "Doormat Mom," said she believes some therapists have contributed to family fractures by focusing too narrowly on one person's experience, when it’s actually a "multi-pronged situation." CUT OFF BY YOUR ADULT CHILD? PSYCHOLOGY RESEARCHER REVEALS WHAT PARENTS SHOULD DO NEXT She said some therapists have even contacted her to reconsider their approach to estrangement cases. "I've had them come to me and ask me, ‘What did we miss?’" she said. Wellington added that she has seen parents encouraged to apologize to their adult children — something she supports when the parent has done something wrong — but believes therapists should consider the broader circumstances surrounding the estrangement. What's driving the divide Differences in values can contribute to family fractures, even in the absence of severe behavior such as violence or abuse, according to Blake. "People are cutting people off because of divergence in values," he said. As one example, Blake pointed to a recent online comment in which someone wrote, "I cut my parents off because they didn't condemn ICE enough." At the same time, he emphasized that there are legitimate circumstances in which ending contact with a parent may be warranted, including physical or sexual abuse. "Then you get into the sort of very murky area of emotional abuse, and this is where therapy culture comes in," Blake added. WHEN IS A MENTAL HEALTH CRISIS TOO SEVERE FOR TELEHEALTH? WARNING SIGNS FAMILIES SHOULDN'T IGNORE The researcher said he believes the term "emotional abuse" is sometimes applied more broadly in therapy and online spaces, particularly in conflicts over politics, religion and language. "Emotional abuse can be [about] differing political values, a little difference in religious beliefs," he said. "It can be about the words people use." "If you don't listen to your child, then don't be surprised if you have conflict with them." What a parent views as legitimate criticism can sometimes be interpreted as emotional abuse by an adult child, according to Blake. "Therapy has sort of raised the bar of what is good enough parenting," he added. "There's just a massive sort of overselling in therapy of how much your parents affected you." In some cases, Blake said, he will hear from parents that their children never told them the issue that led to them being cut off. "They’ll say, ‘We were best friends. And then I got a letter saying, ‘never contact me ever again.’" Blake emphasized, however, that it’s important for parents to listen if the adult child makes an attempt to communicate. 1 IN 6 ADULTS PLAGUED BY LONELINESS AS RESEARCHERS REVEAL LASTING IMPACT OF COVID PANDEMIC "A frequent complaint that most adult children make is, ‘My parents just don't listen. I cannot get through to them. It's like talking to a brick wall,’" he said. "And that is a genuine frustration." "If you don't listen to your child, then don't be surprised if you have conflict with them." Blake recommended active listening techniques, such as allowing the other person to speak without interruption, repeating their concerns back to show understanding, and asking whether they have more to share before offering a response. Blake emphasized that his concerns do not apply to all therapists, saying only a "small subset" may view cutting off family members as an appropriate response to conflict. In situations involving ordinary family conflict rather than abuse, he cautioned that ending contact can have longer-term repercussions even if it initially brings relief. ‘QUIET QUITTING’ IN MARRIAGE: THE SUBTLE SIGNS A SPOUSE HAS EMOTIONALLY CHECKED OUT "It makes you feel good, but there are consequences afterwards — very serious consequences," Blake said. He also challenged the idea that the sole act of cutting off a parent will necessarily resolve underlying mental health struggles. "This is the sort of myth that pervades in cutoff cultures, like, ‘I needed to cut my parents off to protect my mental health,’" he said. The assumption, he added, is: "My parents were the cause of my mental health issues, therefore cutting them out resolves that issue." Other experts have emphasized that people's experiences with therapy during family estrangement can vary. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES Lucy Blake, Ph.D., a developmental psychologist in the U.K. who studies family estrangement, told the American Psychological Association that therapy can be "very helpful" in some cases. "I think people can find therapy very helpful if their therapist has an understanding of estrangement, so some appreciation that it’s rarely one relationship that’s affected when there’s an estrangement," she said. "This is the sort of myth that pervades in cutoff cultures." Therapy can also be beneficial when therapists understand underlying factors that can contribute to family estrangement, such as abuse or mental health challenges, the psychologist noted. Blake has also heard from people who found therapy "very unhelpful," particularly when they felt their therapist lacked warmth and validation or did not understand the "enormous impact" of estrangement and the grief and loss that can accompany it. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Overall, Blake said therapy can be a "really helpful avenue of support" for some, while noting that researchers are "still really learning" what is helpful or unhelpful for people experiencing estrangement. Finding a path forward For families experiencing conflict, bringing in a neutral third party may be a better option when both sides are willing to participate, experts agree. "Communication with a mediator, whether it’s a therapist or a professional mediator, can be really productive," said Richard Blake. Once a family member has already ended communication and asked not to be contacted, however, getting both sides into therapy may no longer be an option. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I certainly think it’s worth a try," he said of mediation. "I know a lot of very good mediators out there who can help people." Wellington agreed that bringing parents and adult children into therapy together could be helpful, although both sides need to be willing to repair the relationship. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ She also added that differing beliefs do not necessarily have to end a relationship. "You can have a different opinion," she said. "You can also have a relationship with your parent who has the other opinion, and that's OK."

articles.title: What we know about apparent attack on Australian MP hit by car
articles.summary: Helen Haines was hit by a car in what the prime minister has called a "deliberate act".
articles.body:
Australian MP Helen Haines has been taken to hospital with critical injuries after she was struck by a car, in what Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has called "a deliberate act".

Haines was hit near an office in Wangaratta, north-east of Melbourne on Monday afternoon local time.

Albanese said counter-terrorism police are involved in the investigation.

Haines was struck by a White Toyota Landcruiser, which was driven by a 43-year-old Tarrawingee man, Victoria Police said.

The suspect was arrested at the scene by a passer-by before being taken into custody by officers, it added.

A knife was also seized from inside the Toyota, the force said.

Victoria Police said it was unknown whether the suspect and Haines knew each other and its investigation remains ongoing.

Haines is a 65-year-old Independent MP for the Indi division in Victoria, south-eastern Australia.

She grew up in the south west of Victoria on a dairy farm with four brothers before training as a nurse and a midwife, according to a biography on her website.

It goes on to say she became the matron of the Chiltern Bush Nursing Hospital in Victoria when she was 26, before later completing a master's degree in public health and a PhD in Medical Science while raising her three children and working. She lives with her family on a small cattle farm outside Wangaratta.

The MP was first elected to the Australian House of Representatives in 2019 and was re-elected in 2022 and 2025.

Australian MP has critical injuries after being hit by car in what PM calls 'deliberate act'

Haines's family said the incident happened outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, a city of about 30,000 people, a few hours north-east of Melbourne in the state of Victoria.

Police said she was hit outside an office on Murphy Street at about 15:35 local time (05:35 BST).

What level of threat is there to Australia's politicians?

Albanese appeared close to tears during a live television interview on ABC's 7.30 programme when he was asked if Australian politicians talk among themselves about the threats and risks they face.

"Yes," he replied, adding: "My concern at this point in time is for one, one of my colleagues."

He later described how there had been a "rise in temperature" and "too much shouting, not enough discourse" in Australia.

Speaking in a news conference, Australian Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said there had been an increase in reports of harassing and threatening behaviour towards lawmakers in the 2025-26 financial year, compared with 951 for the previous year.

Paying tribute to Haines during a news conference, Albanese described her as "incredibly hard-working".

"She is fiercely intelligent but most importantly she is just a thoroughly decent human being full of integrity and respected right across the Parliament and from everyone who comes into contact with her", he added.

He said the attack will come as an "incredible shock" to her community.

Australia's Foreign Minister Penny Wong described the incident as a "shocking and deeply disturbing attack".

The Premier of Victoria Ben Carroll said he was "deeply appalled" by the "violent attack".

Meanwhile, Australia's opposition leader Angus Taylor said he was "deeply saddened and distressed" by the attack.

"This is a shocking day for our nation," he said. "No-one should be targeted in this way."

articles.title: Add a Handful of This Fall Food to Boost Fiber and Antioxidants, Dietitian Says
articles.summary: If you want to add fiber and antioxidants to any meal, a dietitian recommends tossing in just a handful of this tasty fall food. Try it on yogurt and salads.
articles.body: The easiest and perhaps tastiest way to add antioxidants to your fall meals only takes a sprinkle. Just a handful of a certain richly colored, naturally sweet (and tart) fruit can give any meal a boost of healthy plant compounds and fiber, a dietitian says. And the best way to use this ingredient is to simply toss a few of them on top of any meal. Nutrition Tip of the Day: Sprinkle Pomegranate Arils on Meals to Add Fiber and Antioxidants “Pomegranate arils are one of my favorite ways to add antioxidants to everyday meals,” says Natalie Rizzo, registered dietitian and TODAY nutrition editor. Tiny, gem-like pomegranate seeds are packed with healthy plant compounds to support your heart health, she says. And they add a juicy burst of flavor and color to any meal. Why It Matters Pomegranate arils may be small, but they’re full of nutrients that support your heart health, gut health and more. “These juicy little seeds contain polyphenols, plant compounds that help protect cells from oxidative stress and may support heart health,” Rizzo says. Those compounds include anthocyanins, a type of plant pigment also found in blueberries and blackberries that have antioxidant benefits. In fact, pomegranate seeds are among the best fruits for heart health due to these anti-inflammatory compounds, and pomegranate juice is the healthiest fruit juice, some experts say. Pomegranate seeds are “also a good source of fiber,” Rizzo notes. You’ll find nearly 4 grams of fiber in a half-cup serving of arils. And they “add a naturally sweet, tart flavor and satisfying crunch to food,” she adds. How to Get Started Think about sprinkling some pomegranate seeds anywhere you’d like a boost of natural sweetness, nutrients and color. “I love sprinkling them over yogurt, oatmeal, salads or roasted vegetables,” Rizzo says. Try these pomegranate seed recipes: Kale, Mozzarella and Pomegranate Salad with MintYogurt with Honey and PomegranateBrussels Sprouts with Pomegranates, Walnuts and Maple SyrupAvocado Toast With Grapefruit and Pomegranate Seeds Of course, you can carefully remove the seeds from a pomegranate yourself. But, Rizzo notes, you can also buy the arils already removed from the fruit to save time. TODAY’s Expert Tip of the Day series is all about simple strategies to make life a little easier. Every Monday through Friday, different qualified experts share their best advice on diet, fitness, heart health, mental wellness and more.

articles.title: Therapist Laura Berman Says She’s ‘Still Angry’ at Son Who Died at 16 From Overdose
articles.summary: Relationship therapist Laura Berman talks about her new book, “Crying Out Loud,” and her advice for navigating the anger that can come from grief.
articles.body: Relationship therapist Laura Berman has helped countless people navigate through grief as a therapist, but none of her training prepared her for the sudden loss of her own son. Berman announced in 2021 that her son Sam died at 16 after he connected with a drug dealer on Snapchat and bought a pill that was laced with fentanyl and caused him to overdose in his bedroom. Berman found him on the floor and her husband administered CPR but could not resuscitate him. She has now written a book, “Crying Out Loud,” about her experience working through grief over her son’s death, including wrestling with one of its side effects: rage. “You have to move it,” she told Maria Shriver on TODAY Oct. 19. “It will take you out if you don’t move it. Anger turned inward is depression. I’m still angry at Sammy for making such a dumb decision. “I’m angry at myself for whatever I missed or coulda, woulda, shoulda done every minute of that kid’s life,” she added. “And I also know that he wouldn’t want me to blame myself, and that he doesn’t blame me.” “Crying Out Loud,” which comes out Oct. 20, chronicles how grieving her son helped her find a better version of herself. “What I discovered is that grief is like a portal of transformation,” she said. “If you are willing to go into the pain and be with the pain and not run from it and not numb it, it will transform you in beautiful ways.” “I find people stuck in grief, which is all the time, five years out, 10 years out, 20 years out, they are still trying not to feel it,” she continued. “The painful emotions of grief are like waves. And all you need to do is surf them. And that sets you free.” Berman wrote the book for anyone experiencing grief, whether it’s over the end of a relationship, the loss of a job, the death of a loved one or pet, or diminished health. One thing she learned was allowing herself to feel the pain, even if she was in public. “Tears want to come. I’m just going to sit in my car and sob my heart out,” she said. “That will last maybe five minutes. And then it lightens.” Berman started support groups across the country after she and her husband had to learn how to balance grieving their loss while being their for their sons, Ethan and Jackson. “There’s probably an inclination to put on a strong face, be strong for the kids, be something that you’re not, right?” Ethan told Shriver on TODAY. “Don’t hide the meltdowns all the time, you know? You need to be a safe space still for your kid, but also be an honest space.” “I think it’s important to be there for yourself, because if you’re there for yourself, then you can be there for your kids,” Jackson added. Berman said she’s tried to view the grief over Sammy’s loss as a gift. “I like this version of me so much more,” she said. “I have zero tolerance for stupid stuff or things that don’t matter or small talk.” She also cherishes the time she was able to have with her son. “Having Sammy for 16 years and getting to know that beautiful soul was worth it,” she said. “The grief never gets smaller, but we can grow so much bigger around it.” If you or someone you know is struggling with an alcohol, drug or other substance use problem, call the free and confidential helpline of the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration at 1-800-662-HELP (1-800-662-4357), or visit findtreatment.gov.

articles.title: Selena Gomez Says Vaping Is the Reason Her Voice Is Different. What Do Doctors Say?
articles.summary: Selena Gomez has shared that vaping has changed her voice and warned against nicotine use. Here’s how vaping can affect the vocal cords and cause other health problems.
articles.body: Selena Gomez says that vaping has permanently altered her voice. The singer, 34, recently took to social media to address growing speculation online about why she sounds so different. “I’m not going to be able to change my voice,” Gomez said in a video posted to her Instagram Story on Sunday, Oct. 18. “I vaped nicotine a lot. Nicotine is so hard to quit, and I think I just wanted to say, if you’re going through it, or if you’re even trying to vape, it’s just not worth it,” she continued. “It’s so stupid, and it’s changed my voice.” Gomez did not disclose when she started vaping nicotine or for how long. She ended the video by stating that she’s “really excited” because she recently quit. “I stopped, and I just hope we can keep it up. It’s really hard,” the Rare Beauty founder said. The use of vapes among young adults in the United States has increased dramatically over the last decade, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Vaping refers to inhaling mist or aerosol produced by a small handheld device, such as an e-cigarette or vape pen. The aerosol is formed when the vaping device heats up e-liquid, or “vape juice,” which contains a mix of nicotine, flavorings, propylene glycol and other ingredients, per the Cleveland Clinic. The mist, along with particles of these chemicals, is then inhaled into the throat and lungs. Vaping is often marketed as a healthier or “safer” alternative to smoking cigarettes. “There are no safe tobacco products, including e-cigarettes,” the CDC says. Can Vaping Change a Person’s Voice? Yes, it’s possible for vaping to affect a person’s voice, Dr. Paul Kwak, otolaryngologist at NYU Langone’s Voice Center, tells TODAY.com. “People think if they vape, it’s going to be much, much less injurious to the voice. From a vocal health standpoint, it’s not. And the primary reason for that is because it’s hot, dry air on the lining of the airway,” explains Kwak. One’s voice is produced when air from the lungs passes through the larynx, aka the voice box, and the vocal folds or cords, causing them to vibrate. These structures are located top of the airway in the windpipe, Kwak adds, which goes down to the lungs — the same route for vape smoke. Inhaling and exhaling the chemical-filled aerosol can dry out the tissues and mucous membranes of the larynx and trachea and have an inflammatory effect, Kwak says. Good vocal health depends on the ability of the vocal cords to vibrate, he adds, which requires them to be moist and pliable. “When your vocal folds and trachea are dry and inflamed ... you have to work harder to use your voice, so you get often a lot of compensatory muscle tension and strain that can reduce the efficiency of the vocal mechanics, but also change the sound of the voice in very real ways,” Kwak says. The voice may become deeper, hoarser or more gravelly. Vaping can also cause repetitive coughing, which can cause vocal changes, Dr. Anaïs Rameau, otolaryngologist at Weill Cornell Medicine and NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital, tells TODAY.com. These effects are often more noticeable for people who use their voice professionally. “Singers require a level of flexibility, agility and pliability. ... They will start to notice (changes) before non-singers will,” says Kwak. Some vocal fluctuations are normal, especially after an illness. If you notice voice changes or hoarseness that last for more than a week, “it’s a good idea to get checked out,” says Kwak. At the end of her video, Gomez addressed her fans directly about the changes in her voice. “If you guys don’t like listening to my voice, that’s totally understandable. I don’t mind. Just don’t listen to it,” she said. Other Health Effects of Vaping Vaping has been linked to a number of negative health effects, including worsening asthma, damaging the heart and scarring the lungs (aka popcorn lung), per the Cleveland Clinic. It can cause “e-cigarette or vaping product use-associated lung injury” (EVALI), a serious and potentially fatal condition, which was identified in 2019. Plus, vaping may change the airway microbiome, compromising local immunity in the respiratory tract, Rameau adds. Most vapes contain nicotine, a highly addictive chemical compound that can change the way the brain works, leading to more cravings, per the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Nicotine use during pregnancy can damage the heart and brain of a developing fetus. In young people, nicotine may harm brain development and increase the risk of future addiction to other drugs, the CDC says. The aerosols from vapes can contain harmful, cancer-causing chemicals, which enter deep into the lungs. “The data is still preliminary on whether it’s less carcinogenic (than smoking),” says Kwak. Because modern vapes have not been around long enough to study how the effects accumulate over a person’s lifetime, the long-term health consequences of vaping remain unknown. “Adults who have never smoked or used other tobacco products, including e-cigarettes, should not start,” the agency says.

articles.title: More Than 1.5 Million Pounds of Meat and Poultry Recalled Nationwide. See the Full List
articles.summary: More than a million pounds of meat and poultry have been recalled. The recall affects sausages, hot dogs, bacon and deli meats that were sold across the U.S.
articles.body: More than 1.5 million pounds of meat and poultry have been recalled because they may have been affected by a temperature issue during storage. The Kayem Foods Inc. voluntary recall affects hotdogs, sausages, bacon and deli meats sold across the country under brand names like Kayem, Al Fresco, McKenzie, Triple M, Deutschmacher, Jordan’s and more. In total, the company is recalling “approximately 1,584,361 pounds of ready-to-eat (RTE) meat and poultry products because they may have experienced temperature abuse during storage,” according to a recall announcement from the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service. The products were shipped to grocery stores and foodservice locations across the U.S. and in Hong Kong, the FSIS says. People who’ve purchased any of the recalled products should not eat them, the company urges. “Our business depends on providing consumers with safe food of the highest quality,” Matt Monkiewicz, Kayem Foods President and CEO, said in a statement. “Out of an abundance of caution, we are undertaking this voluntary recall.” “We take food safety very seriously and apologize to our valued consumers. Our management team takes full responsibility. We have learned from and corrected the issue and will not allow this to happen again,” the statement continued. Which Products Are Being Recalled? The recall includes a massive list of meat and poultry products. All of the affected products were produced between March 31 and Oct. 7, 2026, the FSIS says. They have a wide range of expiration dates between May 2026 and February 2027. Additionally, products included in the recall will have establishment numbers EST. M/P 7839, EST. P 20935A or EST. M 9520 printed inside the USDA mark of inspection. Some of the products affected by the recall include: Kayem Old Tyme Beef & Pork Frankfurters, SKU#1003 UPC: 003077101003, expiration date Oct. 10, 2026.Al Fresco Roasted Garlic Chicken Sausage, SKU# 2632 UPC: 003077102632, expiration dates between July 26 and Dec. 13, 2026.Triple M Chef’s Delight Tavern Ham, SKU#2977 UPC: 003077102977, expiration date Nov. 3, 2026.McKenzie Cob Smoked Uncured Bacon, SKU#9544 UPC: 003077109544, expiration dates between Aug. 2 and Nov. 25, 2026.Deutschmacher Honey Ham, SKU# 9807 UPC: 003077109807, expiration dates between Aug. 13 and Nov. 12, 2026.Jordan’s Ball Game Treats, SKU# 9813 UPC: 003077109813, expiration date Oct. 17, 2026.Essem Frankfurts, SKU# 9813 UPC: 003077109813, expiration dates between Oct. 22 and Oct. 29, 2026. Winnisimmet Slow Smoked Roasted Bacon, SKU# 9878 UPC: 003077109878, expiration dates between June 14 and Dec. 4, 2026. See the full list of recalled products on the FSIS site. You can also see photos of the products included in the recall here. Why Are the Meat and Poultry Products Being Recalled? Kayem Foods is recalling the meat and poultry due to a temperature issue that occurred during storage. The products are being recalled “due to the recent discovery of a cooling system malfunction at one of the company’s warehouses that resulted in storage temperature deviations,” the company explained in a statement. The issue was discovered after a retail customer complained of “warm product temperatures” at the point of delivery on Oct. 1, the FSIS says. “The establishment investigated and determined that they stored various RTE meat and poultry products in a warehouse cooler that experienced temperature deviations.” There have been no confirmed reports of illness related to eating any of the recalled products, the FSIS notes. What to Do If You Purchased Recalled Products If you purchased any of the recalled hotdogs, deli meats or other products, you should not eat them. Instead, dispose of them or return them to the place where you purchased them, the FSIS says. Additionally, you can contact Kayem Foods at the contact information on its website.

articles.title: Selena Gomez says vaping changed her voice. A doctor warns the effects can last long after quitting.
articles.summary: Selena Gomez took to Instagram to address rumors that her voice sounds different. She said that she "vaped nicotine a lot," which caused the change. An exper...
articles.body:
Selena Gomez is addressing the rumors that she sounds different, with an important message: "I vaped nicotine, a lot," the singer said in an Instagram story . "It's so stupid, and it's changed my voice."

Gomez explained that she's now quit and warned others to stay away from e-cigarettes. "I just wanted to say, if you're going through it or if you're trying to vape, it's just not worth it," the Only Murders in the Building star warned.

Although e-cigarettes are commonly used by people trying to quit smoking, they're not harmless, Dr. Inna Husain , a laryngologist who treats voice issues, tells Yahoo. And many of their effects — including vocal changes — are similar to those of traditional cigarettes.

What's going on with Selena Gomez's voice?

Fans, critics and creators online have been quick to point out the change in Gomez's sound over the years. Many claim her voice now sounds softer and deeper than it once did. Women's voices do change with age, but are typically stable after puberty until perimenopause .

Gomez, who was diagnosed with the autoimmune disease lupus in 2013 , has been asked about her voice before. She attempted to address it during a 2025 Instagram Live, saying: "Yeah, I've gotten this question a few times. The voice thing." Before cutting herself off, she added: "My throat kind of swells inside sometimes." Lupus can cause inflammation throughout the body, including in the voice box, Husain explains. But vaping is just as likely to cause vocal changes and damage.

Vaping is a new enough phenomenon that there isn't a lot of long-term data on its health effects. But, to a laryngologist, it seems "obvious that things like vaping would affect your voice, and it's not just that I see it a lot," says Husain.

Vaping involves inhaling chemicals — from liquids or "e-juices," rather than dry combustible tobacco — that "have to pass through the vocal folds to get to the lungs," says Husain. But many people aren't aware that vaping is similar to smoking in this sense.

The vocal folds are a pair of bands of smooth muscle and soft tissue inside the larynx, or voice box, which vibrate to create the sound of your voice. They're powerful, but fragile. "When the delicate tissue of the vocal folds gets exposed to chemicals … it can trigger a couple of different changes," Husain says.

The first is that these chemicals can cause irritation and inflammation. "Think of it like a wound that needs to heal: Once the tissue is inflamed, the body is going to try to heal … often in the form of what we call remodeling of the tissue," she explains. In other words, the healing process can change the structure of those folds and, with them, the sound that they produce.

Husain also sees patients who vape develop a condition called Reinke's edema . Just under the surface of the vocal cords is what's called Reinke's space, a "kind of protective gel layer," she explains. This tissue can absorb chemicals from smoke or e-cigarette vapor, causing it to swell. The swelling, in turn, can cause parts of the vocal folds to become wider and thicker. "That's going to vibrate differently than if it was a nice, thin and taut kind of vocal fold," Husain says. "So Reinke's edema essentially lowers the pitch of the voice."

Husain says that Reinke's edema is often responsible for the familiar "smoker's voice": a deeper, huskier or more raspy sound. And the demands of being a singer, like Gomez, can both make these changes more noticeable and potentially worsen the damage to the vocal cords.

"She has to sing, but now she's working with a system that's slightly different," says Husain. Gomez might now be "pushing harder than [she used to] to hit the same notes," she adds. That added strain can cause additional injuries, including vocal nodules , which are non-cancerous growths, and ruptures of tiny blood vessels in the cords . These can also affect the quality of the voice, Husain explains.

Can someone's voice recover from vaping?

In short, yes. But it depends on how much they vaped or smoked, for how long and how much damage has been done so far. Like many other tissues, including the lining of the mouth, the vocal folds can "regenerate" to an extent, Husain says. And if someone has only irritation and hoarseness — no nodules or polyps (growths that tend to be fluid-filled or stalk-like and have more blood vessels) — and they quit vaping today, their voice might "bounce back even the next day," says Husain.

But for those who have been vaping or smoking for longer, it can take more time to recover after quitting, and their voice may never be exactly the same. And that's if they can quit, which is notoriously challenging for both smokers and people who vape. One study found that teens who tried to give up vaping were nearly twice as likely to pick the habit up again as smokers who tried to quit.

"Nicotine is so hard to quit," said Gomez in her Instagram story. "But I am really excited because I stopped, and I'm just hoping to keep it up."

Husain acknowledges that quitting is challenging . But rather than going cold turkey, she advises patients who smoke and vape to track how many times they take a puff, and then try to reduce that amount by one or two each day. "Baby steps," she says.

Difficult though it is, Gomez's experience and the data suggest it's well worth quitting. It might not only save your voice, but also reduce your risk of cardiovascular and lung diseases linked to the habit. Gomez urged others to follow her lead through the difficult process of quitting: "I know that if you are going through something, you can get through it too. [But] it sucks," she said.

If you are thinking about quitting smoking or vaping, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has a free helpline. Call 1-800-QUIT-NOW to speak confidentially with a trained coach.

articles.title: The Eagles owe it to Jalen Hurts to address these serious allegations
articles.summary: Conflicting reports about Jalen Hurts' deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary emboli diagnosis raise serious questions about the Eagles' medical decisions.
articles.body: The Philadelphia Eagles' front office ought to address the Jalen Hurts situation publicly, preferably at a press conference. The leaks, PR-approved statements, and secondhand medical analysis aren't helping. If anything, each new development raises further questions about whether medical malpractice occurred. Here's what we know. Hurts was reportedly cleated in his left calf against the Rams on October 4. He first sought treatment on October 8. An ultrasound in London on October 10 revealed a superficial blood clot. Doctors cleared him to play against Jacksonville in London on October 11. Hurts then participated fully in practice on October 14, preparing for the Eagles' game against the Panthers on Sunday. That evening, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the blood clot. On October 15, the Eagles released a statement announcing that Hurts would miss the Panthers game while doctors determined the appropriate course of treatment. The team emphasized that his health and safety were its highest priority but provided no timetable for his return. On Saturday morning, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the Eagles did not plan to place Hurts on injured reserve, which would require him to miss at least four games. The reporting suggested that Philadelphia believed Hurts could return to the field within a month. Later that day, Schefter reported that the Eagles had reversed course and placed Hurts on injured reserve. JALEN HURTS TO REPORTEDLY MISS REMAINDER OF NFL SEASON AFTER BLOOD CLOTS FOUND IN QUARTERBACK'S LUNGS Later that day, Schefter reported that the Eagles had reversed course and placed Hurts on injured reserve. On Monday, The Ringer's Tom Pelissero reported that Hurts was expected to miss the remainder of the season after further medical evaluations revealed a more serious condition. In a joint statement, the Eagles and Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, confirmed that he had been diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning blood clots in both lungs. "Hurts is now on blood thinners and should have no long-term effects," according to the medical prognosis outlined in the statement. In a follow-up report, Pelissero said doctors instructed Hurts not to sleep after discovering the blood clot in London as a precaution. According to the report, Hurts had been awake for roughly 36 hours when he started against the Jaguars. Hours later, amid growing scrutiny from members of the media, Lynn offered a "clarification." Lynn told Pelissero, "Hurts was up until early Sunday morning getting evaluated at a hospital, he was able to sleep upon rejoining the team and the Eagles set aside a room for him at the stadium." John Clark offered a different timeline, reporting Monday that blood clots were discovered in Hurts' lungs on Friday, a day before ESPN reported that the Eagles had no plans to place him on injured reserve. So, what are we to make of all this? At this point, it's difficult to say. The reporting is conflicting, the timeline keeps changing, and each attempt at clarification seems to introduce another layer of uncertainty. Only a small number of people know precisely what happened, including when doctors discovered the clots and whether the Eagles allowed Hurts to play in London after going 36 hours without sleep. Unfortunately, the lack of clarity has made the public discourse worse. Former NFL player Michael Robinson suggested that Hurts was faking the blood clot to avoid playing for a losing team. Meanwhile, doctors analyzing the situation from afar have debated on social media how Hurts' condition should have been treated, often disagreeing with one another. The Eagles owe it to Hurts, their fans, and the integrity of the organization to address these questions directly, in front of reporters. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The handling of Hurts' condition is a serious matter. The reports have raised legitimate questions about whether medical malpractice occurred and whether the Eagles prioritized winning a regular-season game over the health of their franchise quarterback. Those are serious allegations, not established facts. If the Eagles followed appropriate medical protocols and did not expose Hurts to unnecessary risks, they should explain the decisions that led to his clearance and provide the public with a coherent timeline. Doing so would not require disclosing every detail of Hurts' private medical history. It would require accountability and a willingness to answer difficult questions. At this juncture, one thing is clear: the leaks, conflicting reports, and carefully crafted statements have done little to resolve the uncertainty. It has only fueled speculation. articles.title: Lung cancer can grow silently for years, here’s who qualifies for screening
articles.summary: Only 15% of eligible Americans get screened for lung cancer, translating to tens of thousands of preventable deaths every year, doctors warn.
articles.body: Cancer can strike at any age, often without symptoms. For many cancers, routine screening remains the best way to detect the disease early and reduce the risk of death. For lung cancer, screening guidelines can vary, as the disease doesn’t always show obvious signals and can occur in both smokers and never-smokers. Daniel J. Boffa, M.D., chair of the American College of Surgeons Commission on Cancer and a thoracic surgeon at Yale University, noted that lung cancer screening is "one of the most powerful ways" to boost survival. POPE LEO'S LUNG TUMOR RAISES QUESTIONS ABOUT CANCER RISK FOR NONSMOKERS "It reduces the chance of people dying of lung cancer by 20%," he told Fox News Digital. The share of Americans who are eligible for screening but don’t comply translates to "tens of thousands of preventable deaths every year," according to Boffa. "I'm hoping that within four or five years, a screening CT scan will only be confirmatory after they have a positive blood test done at your doctor's office," he added. That approach could make screening easier and potentially help detect more lung cancers, according to the doctor. Potential symptoms In a recent interview with Fox News Digital, Lary Robinson, M.D., an oncologist at Moffitt Cancer Center in Tampa, Florida, noted that in most cases, early-stage lung cancer will not come with any symptoms. In those who do have symptoms, however, the most common are related to the lungs, including a persistent cough, shortness of breath or coughing up blood. DOCTORS PUSH NEW BLOOD TESTS FOR COLON CANCER AS CASES SURGE IN YOUNGER ADULTS Unexplained weight loss can result from any form of cancer, according to the oncologist. Neurological symptoms, like persistent headaches, may also warrant seeing a doctor. Current guidelines Current lung cancer screening guidelines recommend an annual low-dose CT scan for people between the ages of 50 and 80 who currently smoke or have a history of smoking or have at least a 20 pack-year history of smoking, according to the American Cancer Society (ACS). Before making the decision to get screened, individuals should speak with their healthcare providers about the purpose of the screening and how it’s done, as well as the benefits, limits and possible harms, ACS advised. Those who still smoke should be counseled about quitting and offered interventions and resources to help. Individuals with serious health problems that will "likely limit" their lifespan should not be screened, according to ACS, as well as those who won’t be able to get treatment if lung cancer is detected. NEVER SMOKED A CIGARETTE? YOU COULD STILL BE AT HIGHER RISK FOR LUNG CANCER Although one out of seven lung cancers will affect someone who has never smoked, there is currently not a set screening guideline for never-smokers. Finding individuals who would benefit from screening is an "intense area of research," according to Boffa. For now, people with a direct family history of lung cancer without smoking should consider annual screenings, as should higher-risk demographics like Asian women. "I would anticipate that in the next year or two, we will have better guidance for people who are at risk for lung cancer, but never smoked," Boffa predicted. What to expect Boffa noted that advances in lung cancer treatment have improved survival, even at advanced stages, so screening should not be viewed as a pathway to a terminal diagnosis. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "People are really reluctant to be diagnosed with lung cancer because it does carry a stigma," Boffa said. "For years, there was a reputation that it was a terminal diagnosis. It's just been amazing what research has done for lung cancer." CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES Most screenings detect a lung nodule or other abnormality, which is more often an infection, scar or inflammation than a tumor, he said. In about one-third of patients, lung cancer screenings also detect unrelated health issues, including the hardening of heart arteries or a nodule in another part of the body. "The reality is over 99% of nodules are actually benign," Boffa said. "And so, you need to have a conversation about what you are going to do with that information." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I think having that conversation ahead of time is really important so that expectations are set – it's not uncommon to find something. Most of the time, it's not something that's going to affect how long you live." The doctor noted that the CT scan only takes a couple of minutes to perform and does not take place in an enclosed space like an MRI. "People who get claustrophobic usually don't have a hard time with lung cancer screening," Boffa said. "And it usually takes a few days to get a report back." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ For those who are over 50 with a history of smoking, Boffa reiterated that getting screened is "one of the most powerful things you can do to reduce your chances of having your life shortened by lung cancer."

articles.title: Quem era Katiuscia Faria, pediatra que morreu em Goiânia | G1
articles.standfirst: Katiuscia Faria Alves de Oliveira, de 52 anos, trabalhava na Maternidade Nascer Cidadão e no Hemu. A médica passou mal após o último plantão e morreu no sábado (17); a causa da morte não foi esclarecida.
articles.summary: Katiuscia Faria Alves de Oliveira, de 52 anos, trabalhava na Maternidade Nascer Cidadão e no Hemu. A médica morreu após passar mal, e a causa da morte não foi esclarecida.
articles.body:
Pediatra Katiuscia Faria Alves de Oliveira — Foto: Reprodução/Sociedade Goiana de Pediatria

A médica Katiuscia Faria Alves de Oliveira, de 52 anos, que morreu após passar mal em Goiânia , era pediatra dedicada aos cuidados de recém-nascidos, segundo a Maternidade Nascer Cidadão, na capital, onde trabalhava havia anos. Ela cumpriu seu último plantão na unidade na noite de sexta-feira (16), horas antes de passar mal e morrer.

De acordo com a maternidade, Katiuscia atuou na Unidade de Cuidado Intensivo Neonatal (Ucin). No fim da manhã de sábado (17), ela se sentiu mal e foi levada ao Hospital Santa Helena, onde sofreu uma parada cardiorrespiratória e morreu.

Até a última atualização desta reportagem, a causa da morte não havia sido esclarecida.

A morte da pediatra causou comoção entre amigos, familiares e instituições de saúde em Goiás. Em nota, a Maternidade Nascer Cidadão lamentou o falecimento e destacou o legado de amor, dedicação e compromisso da médica com a saúde.

Colegas e familiares lamentam morte da pediatra

Nas redes sociais, amigos e familiares prestaram homenagens a Katiuscia e destacaram o profissionalismo, a dedicação à medicina e a amizade da pediatra.

A médica Paula Pires lamentou a morte da colega e ressaltou as qualidades profissionais e pessoais dela.

“Profissional responsável, trabalhadora, amiga, mãe. Vai fazer muita falta. Estamos desolados”, escreveu.

A irmã da médica, Janaina Faria, também se manifestou sobre a perda repentina.

“Te amo tanto, minha irmã. Está doendo tanto sua partida... ainda sem acreditar... como você era querida e amada”, publicou.

A médica Ana Marcia Guimarães destacou o comprometimento de Katiuscia e a atuação dela no atendimento de emergência.

“Uma pediatra maravilhosa, raiz, verdadeira, salvou inúmeras crianças! A melhor médica na emergência que eu já vi! Responsável, comprometida, estudiosa! Katiuscia, que Deus te receba”, escreveu.

Hospitais e entidades destacam dedicação à medicina

O Hospital Estadual da Mulher Dr. Jurandir do Nascimento (Hemu), onde Katiuscia também trabalhava como pediatra e neonatologista, divulgou uma nota de pesar.

“A sua incansável dedicação às nossas crianças e recém-nascidos deixará uma marca eterna na nossa história e nos nossos corações, permanecendo como um verdadeiro modelo de humanidade, ternura e amor à medicina”, destacou a instituição.

O Conselho Regional de Medicina do Estado de Goiás (Cremego), a Sociedade Goiana de Pediatria (SGP) e a Secretaria Municipal de Saúde de Goiânia (SMS) também lamentaram a morte da médica.

A SMS se solidarizou com familiares e amigos e destacou que a servidora atuava com “compromisso, responsabilidade e espírito de acolhimento, contribuindo de forma significativa para o cuidado e a proteção da saúde da população atendida pelo SUS”.

articles.title: Justiça condena mãe e padrasto por morte de Rhavy Abraão em Maceió | G1
articles.standfirst: Rhavy Abraão Alves de Lima foi morto em maio de 2025 no bairro do Riacho Doce, na capital alagoana. Mãe e padrasto negam ter assassinado a criança.
articles.summary: Rhavy Abraão Alves de Lima foi morto em maio de 2025 no bairro do Riacho Doce, na capital alagoana. Mãe e padrasto negam ter assassinado a criança.
articles.body:
Nicole Maria de Lima Braga e Manoel Pedro Tavares de Souza, mãe e padrastro de Rhavy Abraão — Foto: Anderson Macena/MP-AL

A mãe e o padrasto de Rhavy Abraão Alves de Lima foram condenados, na noite de segunda-feira (19), pelo assassinato do menino, em maio de 2025, no bairro de Riacho Doce, em Maceió .

De acordo com o Ministério Público do Estado de Alagoas (MP-AL), Manoel Pedro Tavares de Souza foi condenado a 50 anos de prisão, em regime inicialmente fechado, pela morte .

Já Nicole Maria de Lima Braga r ecebeu uma pena de dois anos e 11 meses, em regime inicialmente aberto, por omissão .

O corpo de Rhavy foi encontrado dentro da residência do casal em 13 de maio de 2025 . Inicialmente, o caso foi tratado como morte clínica, mas exames cadavéricos identificaram lesões internas.

Um dia após a morte, o Instituto Médico Legal (IML) informou que a criança morreu após sofrer uma ruptura no fígado provocada por agressão . Segundo o órgão, o ferimento foi causado por uma pancada nas costas.

Durante o julgamento, realizado no Fórum do Barro Duro, em Maceió, tanto a mãe quanto o padrasto negaram ter assassinado o menino.

Rhavy Abraão Alves de Lima, de dois anos, foi assassinado em Maceió — Foto: Reprodução

Testemunhas informaram, durante o júri, que as agressões contra Rhavy eram frequentes. Segundo os relatos, Nicole Maria era quem agredia o menino e os outros dois filhos.

A babá da criança, identificada apenas como Viviane, disse que, dias antes do crime, Rhavy se queixava de dor de cabeça. Ela também contou que já havia visto marcas de agressão no corpo do menino em outras ocasiões.

As testemunhas relataram ainda um episódio em que Rhavy teve os olhos colados e precisou ser levado a uma Unidade de Pronto Atendimento (UPA) e, posteriormente, ao Hospital Geral do Estado (HGE), para retirar o material dos olhos.

“Eles iam ao mercadinho e eu vi o olhinho dele [Rhavy] vermelho. Então eu perguntei o que foi e ela [a mãe] disse que ele mesmo tinha colado o olho. Questionei sobre não ter cola na mão dele e ele [o padrasto] disse que não sabia explicar, mas achava que ele mesmo tinha colado o olho”, afirmou Williams da Silva Braga.

Williams, que afirmou ser usuário de drogas, disse que mantinha contato com a família porque comprava entorpecentes de Manoel Pedro.

Tráfico de drogas e tentativa de homicídio

Fórum do Barro Duro, na capital alagoana — Foto: Jonathan Lins/G1

Durante o júri, Manoel Pedro Tavares de Souza afirmou que não trabalhava na época do crime e que atuava no tráfico de drogas na região de Riacho Doce.

Ele também contou que, quando era adolescente, andava armado e foi acusado de tentativa de homicídio, mas acabou absolvido.

“Eu era traficante, mas essas mãos aqui nunca matariam uma criança, até porque nesse meio não é perdoado. Quero que a Justiça seja feita, mas de verdade, e condene quem realmente fez isso com a criança”, declarou.

articles.title: Saiba quem era o médico que morreu em troca de tiros com policiais  | G1
articles.standfirst: Luciano Lopes Pastor foi diretor-presidente do Hospital Psiquiátrico Mahatma Gandhi e já havia sido preso. Polícia apreendeu arsenal de armas e medalha com símbolo nazista na casa dele em Catanduva (SP).
articles.summary: O médico de 52 anos que morreu em uma troca de tiros com a polícia após ameaçar a esposa em Catanduva (SP) no domingo (18) foi diretor-presidente do Hospital Mahatma Gandhi.
articles.body:
O médico de 52 anos que morreu em uma troca de tiros com a polícia após ameaçar a esposa em Catanduva (SP) no domingo (18) foi diretor-presidente do Hospital Psiquiátrico Mahatma Gandhi na cidade e já havia sido preso .

O cirurgião vascular Luciano Lopes Pastor era formado pela Faculdade de Medicina de Catanduva (Fameca), onde estudou entre 1995 e 2001. Ele também era referência no tratamento de angioplastia.

O profissional atendia pacientes em sua clínica particular, localizada no bairro São Francisco. Pelas redes sociais do local, consta que eram oferecidos exames, consultas e escleroterapia (secagem de vasinhos). Segundo apurado pelo g1 , o vascular também atendia no Ambulatório do Hospital Emílio Carlos por meio do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS).

Médico de 52 anos morre em troca de tiros com a polícia, em Catanduva (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Luciano tinha três filhos. Os mais novos, de 10 e 14 anos, são do relacionamento com a atual esposa. O primogênito é fruto de outra relação.

Conforme apurado pela TV TEM , o casal mantinha uma relação estável há 17 anos. A polícia informou que ele não tinha histórico de violência contra mulheres.

A esposa de Luciano acionou a Polícia Militar para denunciar que era vítima de violência doméstica. Ela disse aos PMs ter sido ameaçada de morte pelo médico, que estava armado e agressivo após um churrasco, durante o qual teria ingerido bebida alcoólica.

Quando os agentes chegaram ao local, a esposa já estava fora da casa. Os dois filhos do casal continuaram dentro do imóvel com o pai e se abrigaram no banheiro de um dos quartos.

Ao verificarem que o médico estava armado no portão da residência, os agentes iniciaram o protocolo de negociação. Após a tentativa de diálogo, ele apontou a arma na direção dos policiais e atirou.

Os agentes reagiram e Luciano foi baleado. Ele morreu no local. Um vídeo registrou o som dos disparos no tiroteio . Assista acima.

Os filhos foram retirados da casa sem ferimentos. A mulher do suspeito também não ficou ferida, mas foi levada a um hospital para atendimento, pois estava emocionalmente abalada.

Vídeo registra disparos durante ocorrência policial que terminou com morte de médico em Catanduva (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/Câmera de segurança

Na residência de Luciano, os policiais encontraram um arsenal e uma medalha com o símbolo da suástica nazista . Veja abaixo as armas apreendidas.

Oito armas de fogo, sendo duas espingardas (sem marca aparente), quatro pistolas (uma de calibre 380, duas de marca alemã e outra sem fabricante descrito) e dois revólveres (de calibres 357 e 38);

Seis armas brancas, sendo três espadas, dois espetos e um facão;

98 munições deflagradas de diversos calibres armazenadas em um estojo.

Também foram encontrados um radiocomunicador, um sistema de monitoramento da casa, além da medalha com o símbolo da suástica.

Réplica decorativa de uma granada de mão alemã é apreendida com médico em Catanduva (SP) — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Os policiais também encontraram um objeto semelhante a uma granada. O Esquadrão Antibombas do Grupo de Ações Táticas Especiais (Gate) foi acionado e, após uma análise com o equipamento de raio-x, descobriram que era uma réplica decorativa de uma granada de mão alemã, sem material explosivo.

Como não havia documentação disponível para verificar a regularidade de todas as armas e munições, o material foi apreendido para análise. A arma que estava com Luciano e as armas utilizadas pelos quatro policiais que atiraram foram recolhidas para perícia.

Médico de 52 anos morre em troca de tiros com a polícia, em Catanduva (SP) — Foto: David Santos/TV Tem

Lopes Pastor havia sido preso em 7 de agosto de 2025 , durante uma operação do Gaeco, vinculada ao Ministério Público de São Paulo (MP-SP).

Denominada "Duas Caras", a ação investigava um esquema de corrupção e lavagem de dinheiro envolvendo a gestão de uma Organização Social da Saúde no município, na qual o médico era presidente. Os presos eram ligados à diretoria do Hospital Psiquiátrico Mahatma Gandhi.

Conforme as investigações, o grupo criminoso firmava contratos de gestão com as cidades de Catanduva, Arujá (SP), Carapicuíba (SP), Piracicaba (SP), Viradouro (SP) e Bauru (SP), além de Rio de Janeiro (RJ), Maricá (RJ), Alfredo Chaves (ES), Palhoça (SC), Itapoá (SC), Mafra (SC) e São José (SC).

A partir da gestão das Unidades Básicas de Saúde (UBSs), os suspeitos contratavam empresas terceirizadas que integravam o próprio grupo. Essas empresas emitiam notas fiscais frias e superfaturadas.

Na época, o médico foi liberado e também foi afastado do cargo de diretor-presidente.

Esquema utilizava a Organização Social de Saúde (OS) - Hospital Psiquiátrico Mahatma Gandhi, sediada em Catanduva (SP) — Foto: Monize Poiani/TV TEM

articles.title: Internado com arritmia, Janones anuncia alta hospitalar nesta terça | G1
articles.standfirst: Deputado federal deu entrada no Hospital Vila Nova Star na madrugada desta segunda-feira (19), com arritmia grave e falta de ar.
articles.summary: Deputado federal deu entrada no Hospital Vila Nova Star na madrugada desta segunda-feira (19), com arritmia grave e falta de ar.
articles.body:
O deputado federal André Janones (Rede-MG) anunciou no fim da noite desta segunda-feira (19) que receberá alta hospitalar na tarde desta terça-feira (20).

Internado na UTI do Hospital Vila Nova Star, no Itaim Bibi , em São Paulo , com o quadro de arritmia cardíaca desde a noite de domingo (18) – após a realização do debate da Band – Janones afirmou que vai deixar o hospital durante o início da tarde.

“Amanhã às 13:13 hs em ponto, estarei saindo pela porta da frente do hospital Vila Nova Star em São Paulo para comandar o maior exército democrático do mundo, durante a batalha final! A batalha que conduzirá a Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva à maior vitória de sua vida! Quem viver, verá!!”, escreveu o parlamentar.

O deputado federal é o único administrador do canal “Exército do Lula”, que soma 5,5 milhões de seguidores e é o grande mobilizador da esquerda nas redes sociais neste 2° turno da eleição presidencial. A última publicação foi feita à 0h40. No grupo, o deputado se intitula 'General do Lula'.

"Na saída do hospital, vou aproveitar pra bater um papo pessoalmente com vocês e passar algumas orientações e direcionamentos sobre os próximos passos para a batalha final que se aproxima", escreveu.

Deputado federal André Janones (Rede-MG) anuncia saída do hospital em São Paulo nesta terça-feira (20). — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Segundo o boletim médico divulgado pelo hospital nesta segunda (19), "a evolução clínica de Janones é favorável, com expectativa de alta hospitalar nas próximas 48 horas, caso sejam mantidas as atuais condições de estabilidade".

Até ontem, ele segue na Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI). A internação ocorreu após o debate presidencial entre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), realizado na noite de domingo (18) , na Rede Bandeirantes. Janones acompanhou o encontro presencialmente.

Segundo a assessoria de imprensa do parlamentar, ele deu entrada no hospital por volta das 2h, com um quadro de arritmia grave e falta de ar. A cardiologista Ludhmila Hajjar é a responsável pelo atendimento.

Desde a internação, o parlamentar não se pronunciou nas redes sociais. O último vídeo publicado em seu perfil no Instagram foi na noite de domingo, quando fez uma análise do debate e reclamando de exaustão (veja abaixo).

articles.title: Jalen Hurts diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and blood clots in both lungs: What is pulmonary embolism, why is it dangerous and how is the Eagles quarterback being treated?
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season after doctors diagnosed him with deep vein thrombosis
articles.body: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season after doctors diagnosed him with deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and bilateral pulmonary emboli. The 28-year-old's condition has raised questions about how a blood clot can travel from the leg to the lungs, why it can become dangerous and what recovery involves. The Eagles have said he is clinically stable and expect him to recover fully.What happened to Jalen Hurts?According to the Philadelphia Eagles' official statement, Hurts initially had a superficial blood clot in his left calf. The problem came to light after he reported discomfort following a cleat injury during the October 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams.An ultrasound in London detected the clot before Philadelphia played Jacksonville on October 11. Doctors cleared him to play, according to the team's earlier statement. A follow-up ultrasound after his return to Philadelphia revealed that the clot had moved. Further medical evaluations subsequently identified DVT and blood clots in both lungs.What is deep vein thrombosis?Deep vein thrombosis occurs when a blood clot forms in a deep vein, usually in the leg. It can develop when blood flow slows or a vein becomes damaged.Unlike a bruise or ordinary muscle soreness, DVT can cause complications beyond the injured area. Symptoms may include leg swelling, tenderness, pain, warmth and skin discolouration. However, some people have no noticeable symptoms.The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) explains how these clots develop, who may be at risk and why early medical attention matters.What is bilateral pulmonary embolism?A pulmonary embolism (PE) occurs when a blood clot blocks an artery in the lungs. It often happens when part of a clot from a deep vein breaks away and travels through the bloodstream.The word bilateral means both lungs are affected. However, it does not automatically indicate how severe a person's condition is. The location of the clots, their effect on blood flow and the patient's overall stability all matter.According to the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, symptoms can include sudden breathlessness, chest pain, rapid breathing, a faster heartbeat and fainting. A pulmonary embolism can become life-threatening and requires urgent medical care.Why is Hurts taking blood thinners?The Eagles said Hurts will receive anticoagulant treatment, commonly called blood thinners. These medicines do not literally thin the blood. Instead, they reduce its ability to form clots and help prevent existing clots from growing while the body gradually breaks them down.Treatment requires medical supervision because anticoagulants can increase bleeding risk. The team has also ruled out contact activities, including football, while Hurts undergoes treatment.What does his diagnosis mean for recovery?The Eagles have described Hurts' prognosis as very good and expect a full recovery. However, no specific return date has been confirmed.His case also highlights an important health lesson: being physically fit does not eliminate the risk of blood clots. Injury, reduced blood flow and other medical factors can contribute to clot formation. Long-distance travel may add risk for some people, particularly when other risk factors are present.Anyone experiencing unexplained leg swelling or pain should seek medical advice. Sudden breathlessness, chest pain or fainting requires emergency medical attention. Recognising these warning signs early can make a critical difference.Disclaimer: This article is for general awareness and does not replace professional medical advice. Jalen Hurts' diagnosis and prognosis are based on statements from his team and agent. Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Selena Gomez says nicotine vaping changed her voice after years of use: How addiction, throat irritation and lupus could affect vocal health
articles.summary: Selena Gomez has opened up about a lesser-discussed consequence of nicotine addiction: a change in her voice.
articles.body: Selena Gomez has opened up about a lesser-discussed consequence of nicotine addiction: a change in her voice. The singer and actor recently said she had vaped nicotine heavily and believed the habit had changed how she sounded. Her admission also raises an important health question. Can vaping affect the voice, and how much of a voice change can be linked to nicotine?Selena Gomez admits nicotine changed her voiceIn an Instagram post on Sunday, Gomez said, “I vaped nicotine a lot.” She described quitting as difficult but shared that she had recently stopped using nicotine and hoped to continue.“Nicotine is so hard to quit,” she said, urging people who vape to reconsider the habit. Her message was candid rather than preachy. By acknowledging how difficult quitting had been, she highlighted how dependence can persist even when someone recognises its harmful effects.How vaping may affect the voiceThe voice depends on the vocal cords, two folds of tissue inside the larynx, or voice box. These tissues vibrate as air passes through them, producing sound.Vaping aerosols can irritate the airways and may contribute to throat irritation, coughing and inflammation. These effects can influence vocal comfort and sound. However, evidence does not establish that nicotine alone directly caused Gomez's voice change. The precise cause cannot be determined from her statement.The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) explains that e-cigarette aerosol can contain harmful substances, including tiny particles and chemicals that may be inhaled deep into the lungs. Read the CDC's guidance on e-cigarettes.Lupus may also affect the voiceGomez has lived with lupus, a chronic autoimmune disease that can affect several organs. In a previous Instagram Q&A, she said her throat sometimes swelled internally.Lupus-related inflammation can sometimes affect the larynx and surrounding tissues, potentially causing hoarseness or vocal strain. But it would be inaccurate to assume that lupus explains Gomez's voice change, just as it would be inaccurate to blame vaping alone.Age and other health factors can also change how a voice sounds. A persistent or worsening voice change deserves medical assessment.Why nicotine can be so difficult to quitNicotine is addictive because it affects brain pathways involved in reward and reinforcement. Repeated use can lead to dependence, while stopping may bring cravings, irritability, restlessness and difficulty concentrating.The CDC's guide to quitting smoking explains why quitting can be challenging and outlines ways to seek support. People who vape can speak to a healthcare professional about suitable quitting strategies.A health message beyond celebrity criticismGomez's admission also drew criticism because she received a kidney transplant from her friend Francia Raisa in 2017 after complications associated with lupus. However, public comments alone cannot establish how vaping has affected her kidney health.The more useful lesson is not to shame someone for addiction. It is to recognise that nicotine dependence can be difficult to overcome and that seeking help is a practical step towards better health.

articles.title: The road to recovery after spinal cord injury: Why neuro-rehabilitation matters
articles.summary: A person life changes in seconds once they suffer from a spinal cord Injury A fall, road accident or sports injury may leave someone unable to move their
articles.body: A person life changes in seconds once they suffer from a spinal cord Injury A fall, road accident or sports injury may leave someone unable to move their legs, sit without support or manage basic daily tasks. Surgery is often the first priority because the spine needs to be stabilised and protected from further damage. But surgery is not the only aspect, another important phase begins post operation. That is where neuro-rehabilitation comes in.For a person with spinal cord injury, recovery is not simply about getting the spine to heal. It is about helping the body make the best possible use of the function that remains, while retraining movement and everyday skills. This process is often long, demanding and, at times, frustrating. Yet, with a structured rehabilitation plan, even small improvements adds up to meaningful independence.Taking example of a recent case gives a better idea about the importance of rehabilitation. A 40-year-old man suffered a fall during a holiday in Manali. He fractured his first lumbar vertebra and sustained a severe spinal cord injury. He lost movement and sensation in both legs and underwent emergency spinal surgery in Delhi. The surgery stabilised his spine, but he remained paralysed below the waist.When he subsequently began an intensive neuro-rehabilitation programme, even basic activities were difficult. He could not sit, stand or walk independently and needed substantial assistance with dressing, bathing and toileting. His rehabilitation therefore had to go beyond simply trying to make him walk again.Rehabilitation doesn't mean doing a task again and again. It is structured program led by a Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (PM&R) doctor who are also called a physiatrist. They lead the rehabilitation teams including physical and occupational therapists to guide the patient recovery". Physiotherapy, focuses on improving muscle strength, balance and movement. Occupational therapy which helps patients relearn practical tasks such as dressing, transferring from bed to a chair and managing personal care. Rehabilitation nursing helps with bowel and bladder care, skin protection and other complications.Technology can add another layer to this process. Robotic gait training, functional electrical stimulation, sensor-based balance exercises and virtual reality can provide repetitive and controlled practice. The aim is not to replace hands-on therapy, but to give patients more opportunities to practise movements safely and consistently.A key concept behind this approach is neuroplasticity; It is the term the used to highlight the nervous system's ability to adapt and reorganise in response to injury. Repetition matters. When a same movement is repeated again and again, the brain and the nervous system receive repeated signals associated with that task. Rehabilitation uses this core principle through structured, goal-based exercises rather than leaving recovery to time alone.The Manali patient gradually demonstrated what this approach can mean in practical terms. Over the course of rehabilitation, muscle strength in both lower limbs improved from 0/5 to 4/5 on clinical muscle testing. Sensation also began returning, along with improvements in bladder and bowel awareness. He regained independence in bed mobility, developed good sitting balance and progressed to standing with supervision. He was eventually able to walk indoors, including to the bathroom, with supervision.The larger lesson is that spinal surgery and neuro-rehabilitation serve different but connected purposes. Surgery stabilises the injury and Rehabilitation works towards improving function, preventing complications and helps the patient adapt to life after the injury.Recovery after spinal cord injury rarely follows a straight line. Some days bring visible progress; others may seem unchanged. That does not make the rehabilitation process any less important. The goal is to keep building on whatever function is possible and turn clinical gains into practical independence.Surgery may mark the beginning of treatment, but it should not be the end of recovery. The road continues through months of focused rehabilitation, and with the right support, a simple progress which may seem not much gradually helps in complete recovery.Dr. Amit Dhumale, Director- Rehabilitation, Jupiter Hospital, ThaneGet the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates.
