articles.title: Luis Enrique, entrenador del PSG: “He llegado a cenar seis huevos. Es uno de los alimentos con más nutrientes, nunca falta en mi dieta”
articles.standfirst: Esta es la rutina de uno de los mejores entrenadores del mundo
articles.summary: Esta es la rutina de uno de los mejores entrenadores del mundo
articles.body: Para estar en la cima, hace falta motivación, pasión por tu trabajo y una buena salud. Luis Enrique aúna todas las características y su PSG es ya historia del fútbol reciente. El equipo francés ha ganado dos Champions consecutivas con el técnico asturiano al mando. Esta temporada 2026-2027 va en busca del ‘three peat’ que sólo ha conseguido el Real Madrid de Zidane en la etapa actual de la competición. Para llegar por buen camino, Luis Enrique deberá vencer, por ejemplo, al Barcelona. Este martes, 20 de octubre, a las 21:00, el equipo de Flick se enfrenta al PSG en el que se está convirtiendo en uno de los clásicos del fútbol europeo. La temporada pasada, a estas alturas, también se encontraron. Aquel partido se cerró con victoria para los franceses por 1-2. El caso es que Luis Enrique no sólo es un enamorado del fútbol. También guarda grandes enseñanzas de la alimentación y rutinas de ejercicio físico. En el documental ‘No tenéis ni pu** idea’ se hizo un viral un vídeo en el que, cada 30 minutos, sonaba una alarma en su teléfono para hacer una serie de ejercicios para mantener su cuerpo activo. Cuando abrió su propio canal de Twitch con la Selección, también reveló alguna de sus costumbres a la hora de ingerir alimentos: “He cenado seis huevos, tres cocidos y tres fritos, judías verdes, zanahoria, boniato y de postre un yogur. Y en los días prepartido nos tomamos una cervecita. Es un ritual. La verdad es que no se puede tener una energía mejor”. Algunos usuarios le preguntaron si, realmente, comer esa cantidad de huevos era sano. El técnico asturiano se reafirmó: “Seis huevos y más, es uno de los alimentos con más nutrientes”. Además, también reveló que come muy poco pan por los hidratos de carbono.

articles.title: ‘Super-drug’ 10 times stronger than fentanyl linked to deaths across multiple states
articles.summary: Cychlorphine, a synthetic opioid reportedly up to 10 times more potent than fentanyl, has been linked to at least 55 deaths across the U.S.
articles.body: A powerful new synthetic opioid said to be more potent than fentanyl has been linked to dozens of recent deaths in the U.S., prompting warnings from health officials. Tennessee was an early hotspot, with the state’s health department announcing in March that more than 30 fatal overdoses had been associated with cychlorphine since October 2025. An April 2026 notice from the White House’s Office of National Drug Control Policy cited at least 41 Tennessee deaths between July 2025 and February 2026 and at least 55 deaths nationally. KRATOM INDUSTRY WARNS SYNTHETIC OPIOIDS SHOULD NOT BE CALLED 'KRATOM' Fatal overdoses have also been reported in Illinois, California and Oklahoma, according to public health and law enforcement records. "Cychlorphine is particularly dangerous due to its strength, where a very small amount can cause someone to stop breathing," the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health said in its advisory. Nicholas Kardaras, Ph.D., CEO and chief clinical officer of the New York Center for Living in Manhattan and a clinical professor at Stony Brook Medicine’s School of Social Welfare, called cychlorphine "the new fentanyl on steroids." WHAT TO KNOW ABOUT PENTOBARBITAL AFTER DEATH ROW INMATE SURVIVES 2 LETHAL INJECTION DOSES Cychlorphine is a novel, unregulated synthetic opioid that activates the same receptors as fentanyl, according to the Drug Enforcement Administration. It can cause profound sedation, slowed or stopped breathing, or death. The drug is not approved for medical use and has been detected in illicit drugs and counterfeit pills. Kardaras called cychlorphine "one of the most potent synthetic opioids" now appearing in the illicit drug supply. "Fentanyl is about 50 times more potent than morphine or heroin," he told Fox News Digital. "Cychlorphine is reportedly up to 10 times more potent than fentanyl — so theoretically, about 500 times more potent than morphine or heroin." "This new synthetic drug is making fentanyl look like yesterday's candy." DR DREW PINSKY REVEALS RED FLAG IN PRESLEY GERBER ADDICTION TREATMENT BEFORE MODEL'S DEATH Cychlorphine is taken in various forms — people can ingest it as a pill, snort it in powder form or crush it and administer it intravenously, according to Kardaras. "The problem has been, in addition to its potency, it's often put in other designer drugs and in counterfeit pills," he cautioned. "It's a constant battle of keeping up with the latest iterations of new drugs." While some people seek out cychlorphine for its potency, others may ingest it unknowingly when it is mixed into other substances. "Sometimes, by talking about how potent some of these substances are, we increase the allure of them for some addicts, unfortunately," Kardaras said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES While cychlorphine is primarily a street drug, it can also be purchased online or via "boutique designer-drug markets," according to the expert. Cychlorphine can cause a fatal overdose in anyone, regardless of age. Kardaras said younger people may face greater exposure because some are more likely to experiment with drugs or purchase counterfeit pills. "They’re buying something online … and all of a sudden, without knowing it, they’re ingesting fentanyl or another synthetic opioid," he said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Naloxone, commonly sold under the brand name Narcan, can reverse cychlorphine’s opioid effects, but multiple or prolonged doses may be needed. "What used to take one or two doses of Narcan to reverse an overdose may now require five or six doses, based on anecdotal evidence," Kardaras said. The DEA advises people to administer naloxone immediately, call 911 and be prepared to give additional doses. Another major concern with cychlorphine is that standard fentanyl test strips and routine hospital opioid urine screens do not detect it. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "Most drug tests have very specific chemical structures that they detect in any kind of synthetic or non-synthetic drug, and this new one hasn't quite been baked into the current testing strips," Kardaras noted. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The takeaway, he said, is that cychlorphine may be up to 10 times more potent than fentanyl, is not detected by standard fentanyl test strips or routine hospital opioid urine screens, and may require multiple doses of naloxone to reverse. "So it's a triple whammy," he said. "It's a constant battle of keeping up with the latest iterations of new drugs."

articles.title: DR MARC SIEGEL: Iowa's cancer rate is rising. One answer may be found in the water
articles.summary: Iowa's cancer rate is 10% above the national average, and nitrates from fertilizer and manure in drinking water are drawing scrutiny from MAHA and RFK Jr.
articles.body: There is a growing concern in Iowa that the increasing cancer rate (10% over the national average, including rates of prostate, breast, colorectal, melanoma and lung cancer) at a time when cancer onset is decreasing in all but three states, could be associated in part with toxins in the environment. Iowa is a big producer of corn and soybeans and also raises hogs. Corn and soy production leads to nitrogen runoff, which can end up in river water used for drinking. The EPA doesn’t yet list nitrates, which come from chemical fertilizers and animal waste, as carcinogens, but they can be converted inside the human body via nitrosation into probable carcinogens. At the same time, there is concern about the use of pesticides and "forever chemicals." The Make America Healthy Again movement, led by HHS Secretary RFK Jr., has put its big thumb on the scale in favor of decreasing exposure to these chemicals. Candidates on both sides of the political aisle are jumping on board. CAN FAITH HELP PATIENTS HEAL? VETERAN DOCTOR REVEALS WHAT HE'S WITNESSED FIRSTHAND MAHA Action President Tony Lyons told me that the need to decrease chemical exposure is crucial and that not all politicians in Iowa are as sincerely committed to change. He said that numerous studies have linked contaminated water, loaded with nitrates from fertilizer and manure, to cancer. Studies have also linked chemicals in many pesticides "to higher risk of colorectal, bladder, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and other cancers." As Republican gubernatorial candidate Zach Lahn has said, "Any discussion that does not include water quality and the nitrate load when we’re talking about cancer isn’t a serious discussion. It doesn’t matter if you’re left or right, you’re drinking the water." Keep in mind that state-funded research at the University of Iowa still shows that most — but not all — of Iowa's above-normal rates for several cancers can be explained by demographic and behavioral factors, such as smoking and binge drinking. Linda Jacobs, age 64, is a direct recipient of a medical miracle resulting from this research. She, along with her medical angel, Mohammed Milhem, MBBS, could easily have stepped right off the pages of my new book, "The Angels Among Us." A decade ago, she had recurrent breast cancer necessitating a bilateral mastectomy and radiation therapy. Unfortunately, she developed an extremely aggressive and unresponsive angiosarcoma. Milhem injected her tumor with a genetically altered herpes virus he has been studying, and it rendered her cancer-free. articles.title: María Ángeles Rol, catedrática de Fisiología, sobre el cambio de hora: "El horario de invierno es más beneficioso"
articles.standfirst: Los expertos recomiendan, de nuevo, un horario único
articles.summary: Los expertos recomiendan, de nuevo, un horario único
articles.body: Apenas faltan unos días para que España vuelva a cambiar la hora y la sociedad deba, de nuevo, amoldarse a lo que esto supone. La madrugada del sábado al domingo, 25 de octubre, a las tres de la mañana serán las dos. Esto sigue la normativa europea, que establece esa modificación para adaptar el horario de invierno para el último fin de semana del mes de octubre. Desde hace años, el debate sobre qué horario sería mejor, en caso de adoptar uno único, está sobre la mesa. La mayoría de los expertos, eso sí, se inclina por el horario de invierno. Una postura que choca con lo expresado en abril por los ciudadanos españoles, según datos del Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas (CIS): el 65% prefiere el de verano. María Ángeles Rol de Lama, catedrática de Fisiología, defiende los motivos de que el horario de invierno se implante: “Desde el punto de vista de la cronobiología, el horario de invierno es más beneficioso porque va más acorde con los ciclos de luz y oscuridad”, dice en palabras recogidas por El País. Los expertos consideran que si se apostara por el horario de verano, la conducta del ser humano cambia por completo: la luz repercute en el consumo de sustancias como el alcohol o el tabaco. “Recibimos más luz durante el horario escolar y laboral, que beneficia a la concentración, y hay más oscuridad por la noche, lo que nos ayuda a conciliar el sueño”, asegura Emilio J. Sánchez Barceló, fisiólogo. “Empeora el sueño, pero también empeora el rendimiento, por ejemplo, al volante, y se aprecia un aumento moderado de eventos cardiovasculares”, sostiene en un nuevo argumento Rol de Lama, cuya postura está del lado de la Comisión Nacional para la Racionalización de los Horarios Españoles , ARHOE: “Promueve un ritmo biológico más estable que el de verano”.

articles.title: Man to stand trial over murder of woman in 1994
articles.summary: Fraser Kilpatrick is accused of killing Shona Stevens close to her home in North Ayrshire 32 years ago.
articles.body:
A man is to stand trial over the murder of a woman in North Ayrshire more than 30 years ago.

Fraser Kilpatrick allegedly killed Shona Stevens, 31, after striking her with a hammer or similar weapon near her home in Irvine in November 1994.

The 68-year-old, who was charged over her death last year, also faces 15 other charges including the rape of a woman and a young girl between 1986 and 2001.

Kilpatrick denies the claims. Lord Arthurson set a date for the trial to begin in January 2028 at the High Court in Glasgow.

The trial is expected to last about 17 days.

A further hearing is scheduled to take place in December this year.

Man charged over Shona Stevens murder in 1994

Novelty keyring bid to solve 1994 cold case murder

Stevens, a mother of one, had been a student at what was then the University of Paisley.

She had walked through Bourtreehill Park to get to the nearby Co-op store at Bourtreehill Shopping Centre at about 13:10 on 10 November 1994.

On her walk back through the park, she was attacked and suffered severe head injuries.

Stevens was found in a wooded area near her home a short time afterwards and was taken to then Southern General Hospital in Glasgow.

She died as a result of her injuries three days later.

Police released several appeals for information over the next 31 years and the case featured on an episode of BBC Crimewatch .

Officers launched Operation Short in 2021, which included the release of images of a keyring found near the scene.

Stevens' daughter, Candice, was aged just seven at the time of her death.

Kilpatrick, of Glasgow, was arrested and charged in July 2025 , a year after a Crimestoppers appeal offered a £20,000 reward for any information linked to the case.

Kilpatrick is also charged with a number of other offences.

He is alleged to have raped a woman who has since died, and a young girl, on various occasions.

Kilpatrick faces accusations of physically assaulting both of them, including punching and kicking the woman, causing her to fall down a flight of stairs.

He allegedly struck her with several household items, brandished a knife at her, choked her, and struck her with a screwdriver to the danger of her life.

He is also accused of similar behaviour towards a young boy and wilfully ill-treating children including exposing them to drugs and forcing them to drink alcohol.

Kilpatrick faces further allegations of lewd and libidinous behaviour, attempting to rape and physically assaulting another girl.

He is accused attempting to induce the girl to take part in sexual activity with an unknown man.

Kilpatrick also allegedly attacked another young girl, including claims he touched her inappropriately and poured boiling water on her body.

He is separately alleged to have tried to hit a man on the head with a hammer, wielded a baseball bat at a woman, and brandished a knife at two people.

His lawyer, Donald Findlay KC, told Lord Arthurson that Kilpatrick pleaded "not guilty to the various charges against him".

Advocate depute, Alex Prentice KC, representing the prosecution, said discussions over the case had been going on "for a long time".

Lord Arthurson recommended that a judge be allocated for the case as it goes through the court process.
